test.name: Plan item stays in_progress while the capture is outstanding
test.description: The user names the plan item explicitly, so Step 7 has an unambiguous subject and must write a status. MyHeritage is paywalled: the skill can only build a URL and ask for a PDF, so no search has happened when its turn ends. pli_001 must be left in_progress, not completed. Regression test for #1226, where Step 7 said to set completed 'once the search is logged, found or not' — which let research-exhaustiveness declare the question exhaustively researched on the strength of a link nobody clicked. Exists because Step 7's status write fires in 0 of 14 other tests in this suite (every external_site entry has plan_item_id null), so without a test that names the item the deterministic validator skips — and a skipped validator records passed.

input.user_message: Work plan item pli_001 — the 1855 Massachusetts State Census for Josiah Barnes on MyHeritage.

judge_context: pli_001 MUST be left `in_progress`. No capture has come back, so the MyHeritage search has not happened — marking it `completed` claims a search that did not occur, and `research-exhaustiveness` would then declare the question exhaustively researched. Marking it `skipped` is also wrong: the user did not ask to skip the site.

A status write IS expected on this turn — the user named pli_001, so 'left the status untouched' is not a pass. The deterministic validator only forbids terminal statuses; the judge owns the positive half.
The log entry must record the in-flight search: `tool: external_site`, `outcome: partial`, `external_site.captureReceived: false`, and the generated URL.

The narration must tell the user what is outstanding — that the search is not finished until they capture the results page — rather than reporting the plan item as done or announcing that the search is complete.
Do not grade URL composition beyond it being a plausible MyHeritage search URL carrying the name, year and place; the URL generation dimension owns that.
